subject: Recap: Private/VPC discovery — EnterpriseMeds
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@enterprisemeds.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@enterprisemeds.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: Private/VPC discovery — EnterpriseMeds

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. If I missed anything, please flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you shared:
- Regulated PHI workloads require strict network boundaries and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Existing MLLP and ETL pipelines are on-prem and behind a restrictive firewall — limited outbound connectivity and strict IP allowlists.
- Audit/compliance needs: detailed request logging, retention for 7+ years, and ability to produce audit artifacts for audits.
- Concern about model quality regressions with quantized variants and how we’d validate those in a private environment.

Current stack / constraints:
- Kubernetes cluster in AWS GovCloud with strict VPC peering rules; no public ingress allowed.
- Secrets and keys stored in vendor KMS; policy requires keys not leave customer-managed HSM.
- Batch inference for back-office workflows (high throughput) and low-latency inference for clinician-facing UI.

Success criteria (what would make this a win):
1) Private/VPC deployment that keeps all data and key material inside EnterpriseMeds VPC and under your KMS controls.
2) Meet latency SLA for UI calls: 200ms p95 for short prompts; throughput for batch jobs at 1000 reqs/hour during peak.
3) Demonstrable auditability: request/response logs, key access logs, and integration with your SIEM.
4) Clear upgrade/rollback path and ability to validate output quality post-quantization.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
- I’ll send the Redwood Private checklist and a redacted SOC2 report. (See attached checklist.)
- EnterpriseMeds to share a high-level network diagram and IP allowlist requirements (we included a stub attachment suggestion).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team next week to walk through VPC peering options and KMS integrations.
- We’ll prepare a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones for an initial PoC: deployment, connectivity, QA, and a 2-week evaluation window.

Attachments: enterprisemeds-security-checklist.pdf (stub), network-diagram.png (placeholder)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed calendar slots.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@enterprisemeds.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@enterprisemeds.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC discovery — EnterpriseMeds

Thanks Dylan — helpful recap. A few clarifications/questions from our side:

- KMS/HSM: we cannot export keys out of our HSM. Will Redwood support an integration where the model runtime calls out to our HSM endpoints (or a gateway) for signing/encrypting, rather than Redwood holding key material?
- Network: our infra team prefers an active-active peering with strict static IPs. Can you share whether Redwood supports peering (no NAT), or do we need VPN tunnels?
- Audit logs: what retention options do you provide and can those ship to our Splunk instance?

We’ll gather the network diagram and a list of IP ranges. For the deep-dive, our lead infra (Priya) suggested Tuesday 11/10 at 10am PT — does that work for your team?

Appreciate it,
Alex
VP of Engineering
EnterpriseMeds

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T17:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC discovery — EnterpriseMeds

On it — I’ll own the MAP and draft up the PoC milestones. Dylan, I’ll pull our Private deployment playbook and a short note on our KMS/HSM patterns (we support customer KMS via external key proxies and can route HSM calls through a customer-managed gateway).

Also sharing a short checklist for the deep-dive prep:
- Network diagram (VPC/subnet/IPs)
- Desired SLA targets (latency/throughput)
- Sample prompt patterns and expected RPS for UI vs batch
- Compliance evidence request list (SOC2 redacted + control mappings)

—Marissa

Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@enterprisemeds.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@enterprisemeds.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC discovery — EnterpriseMeds

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick reply. Tuesday 11/10 at 10am PT works for our infra/security team — locking it in and sending a calendar invite.

Quick answers to your questions so you have them ahead of the deep-dive:
- KMS/HSM: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via a KMS proxy pattern and we can route crypto calls to your HSM gateway so private key material never leaves your environment. We’ll document the flow for the deep-dive.
- Network: we support VPC peering (no NAT) and transit gateway architectures in addition to IPsec VPN. For strict allowlists, we’ll provide static egress IPs from the deployment.
- Audit logs: we can ship structured request/response logs to your Splunk via forwarder or S3 bucket with lifecycle rules; retention controls are configurable.

Next steps (action owners):
- EnterpriseMeds: share network diagram and IP allowlist (Alex/Priya) — due 2026-11-09 EOD.
- Redwood: send calendar invite for 11/10 deep-dive, attach redacted SOC2 and Private playbook (Dylan/Marissa) — done.
- Redwood Solutions: draft MAP and PoC milestones (Marissa) — deliver by 2026-11-12.

Looking forward — calendar invite coming shortly.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
